Classification

Obsessive-compulsive or related disorders

CIE-11: block 6B20–6B2Z · look up in ICD-11 ↗
DSM-5-TR: Obsessive-compulsive and related disorders

They share intrusive thoughts or repetitive worries and behaviours the person feels they must carry out to relieve distress: checking, cleaning, ordering, looking in the mirror, hoarding, pulling out hair. People often recognise that it is excessive but find it very hard to stop.

An interesting difference: ICD-11 places hypochondriasis in this group, because of its resemblance to obsessions, whereas DSM-5-TR includes it as "illness anxiety disorder" in the somatic symptom chapter. ICD-11 also adds olfactory reference disorder: a persistent preoccupation with smelling bad.

What it includes

  • Obsessive-compulsive disorder
  • Body dysmorphic disorder
  • Olfactory reference disorder
  • Hypochondriasis
  • Hoarding disorder
  • Body-focused repetitive behaviour disorders (trichotillomania, excoriation)
